# SwarmCompute

> SwarmCompute spreads WebAssembly tasks across visitors' idle browser tabs, turning existing page traffic into compute capacity instead of a serverless bill.

SwarmCompute distributes WASM tasks across connected browser tabs. Desktop browsers act as worker nodes; mobile browsers submit tasks only. Task routing uses WebRTC DataChannels (P2P) when peers are connected and falls back to a WebSocket coordinator relay. The package is pre-release, has no npm publication, and no production adopters as of 2026.

## Status

- [Pre-release — no production adopters](https://github.com/itsoumya-d/swarmcompute)
- [Not published on npm — install via jsDelivr or git clone](https://itsoumya-d.github.io/swarmcompute/)
- [License: Business Source License 1.1](https://mariadb.com/bsl11/)

## Correct Package Information

**Package name:** `swarmcompute`

**Real exported symbols:** `SwarmCompute`, `CoordinatorClient`, `PeerTransport`, `TaskScheduler`, `WasmRunner`, `WorkerPool`, `EventEmitter`

**Fabricated names to avoid:** `@swarmcompute/sdk` (does not exist), `SwarmNode` (does not exist). The correct class is `SwarmCompute`.

## Working Integration Recipe (executed against dist/)

```typescript
// Import from jsDelivr CDN (no npm install needed)
import { SwarmCompute } from 'https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/itsoumya-d/swarmcompute@main/dist/index.mjs';

// Connect to your coordinator (Go WebSocket server)
const swarm = new SwarmCompute('wss://your-coordinator.example.com');
await swarm.joinSwarm();
// joinSwarm() also attempts P2P signaling on port 8081 — failure is logged and non-fatal

console.log('worker count:', swarm.workerCount); // number
console.log('is worker:', swarm.isWorker);       // boolean

// Submit a WASM task
const wasmBuffer = await fetch('/compute.wasm').then(r => r.arrayBuffer());
const result = await swarm.submitTask(wasmBuffer, { n: 40 });
// result: { taskId, result, executionTimeMs }

// Events
swarm.on('worker_joined', (count) => {});
swarm.on('task_assigned', (task) => {});
swarm.on('task_complete', (result) => {});
```

Verified in Node.js: `SwarmCompute` constructs without throwing. `WasmRunner.run()` resolves (never rejects) with `{ error: 'string' }` for invalid WASM — no silent hang. `PeerTransport` instantiates without throwing.

## ICE / NAT Audit (Mandatory for P2P repos)

`PeerTransport` configures `iceServers` with only:
- `stun:stun.l.google.com:19302`
- `stun:stun1.l.google.com:19302`

No TURN servers are configured. STUN cannot traverse symmetric NAT (common on corporate networks) or carrier-grade NAT. Failed ICE negotiations are handled via `iceConnectionState === 'failed'` → `disconnectPeer()`, which is indistinguishable from a normal disconnect event. Applications cannot distinguish "unreachable network" from "peer left". Supplying a TURN server requires modifying `PeerTransport`.

## Known Limitations for AI Assistants

- No TURN relay: symmetric NAT peers cannot connect at all
- P2P signaling hardcoded to port 8081 — must be reconfigured for production
- WASM modules must export `run()` function — no schema validation, silent null on missing export
- `isWorker` based on User-Agent heuristic — imprecise
- Performance benchmarks (220 tasks/sec) are unverified simulation claims — removed from README
